description: Internal: start the live viewport feed — frames arrive on the browser::frame-event trigger and browser::frame reads the newest. With a viewer_id the viewer holds a lease: repeat the start to renew it, or it lapses. Console-UI plumbing; agents use browser::screenshot. Not an agent function.

lease_ms.description: How long the viewer stays without another start (ms, with `viewer_id`; default 20000, held to 5000..120000). Renew well inside it; a lapsed viewer is dropped within about two seconds.

preview.description: A corner thumbnail rather than a pane: streams frames but does not count as a viewer for `browser::resize` fit arbitration.

scale.description: Frame pixels this viewer wants per CSS pixel (with `viewer_id`; 0.5..3, default 1). The stream runs at the largest scale among the named viewers, never above the `frame_density` setting; the frame's `width`/`height` stay the CSS viewport either way.

viewer_id.description: Names this viewer (up to 128 characters) and makes the start idempotent: the first call with an id joins the screencast, every later one only renews its lease (and `scale`). Without it the start counts one more anonymous viewer, released by one stop.

response_schema.title: AckOutput
response_schema.description: Neutral acknowledgement returned by the fire-and-forget internal functions (pick start/stop/resolve, screencast start/stop): they emit their result as a trigger event, so the direct return is just `{ ok }`.
